brief.purpose: find the weak link in this dependency graph and trace the relationships around it

constraints: the dependency graph is the evidence, not a list

direction.rationale: 7 composition hypotheses proposed across 7 families — each pair differs on at least one structural axis of §4.1 (audited: distinct). | Task-category weights from the shared table, keyed directly by the decision class. | Selected 'spatial' (6.48/100) over 6 alternative(s); Chose "spatial" over "table" (6.48 vs 6.44). Gains: relationshipClarity. Gives up: informationHierarchy, densityScanability.. | Steering: the planner receives 'spatial' as its desiredComposition hint, under its own viability rules — the planner may still conclude the roles in play cannot support it.

skills.why: visual-intent.numerals: 2 information item(s) name numeric readouts; tabular numerals keep updating and compared values aligned.; visual-intent.alignment: No readout-dense task; alignment stays loose so the editorial rhythm carries.; visual-intent.alignment overridden: The compiler applied type-and-space's value (No readout-dense task; alignment stays loose so the editorial rhythm carries.). The overridden decision stays here for audit.

archetype: Finding is narrowing a list and looking at one of them; list-detail is the honest shape of that. Content shape: 7 information item(s), numeric readouts present, spatial request not stated.; focal-role: The archetype names what the eye is for, so the plan's focal can be checked against it.; rejected:canvas: Stated so the composition is a decision, not the absence of one.; visual-intent.density: From the archetype's density rule for this decision figure and content shape; overridden by a composition descriptor when the direction states one.; visual-intent.rhythm: The archetype's whitespace contract; overridden by a composition descriptor when the direction states one.; visual-intent.alignment: Numeric scanning rewards strict grid alignment; tune up alignment when values update in place.

discoveries: Readable-numeral decision: tabular numerals for the 2 numeric readout item(s).

Type-role contract: the screen name takes the title role, the decision context takes the subtitle, each information item takes its natural role (eyebrow for metadata, label for chrome-ish captions, body for prose, code for identifiers), and status states take the label role at legible size.

Acceptance criteria declared: no label below 11px; uppercase reserved for eyebrows; one spacing rhythm step between sibling regions; body columns around 75 characters. Measured on rendered evidence when screenshot critique runs (issue #22 phase 2).
Composition archetype contract: list-detail (planner runs after this and derives regions; the plan is reviewed against this contract).
Field conflict on 'visual-intent.alignment': 'visual-intent.alignment'='strong' from composition-strategy overridden by type-and-space's decision; overridden decision kept in the trail.
Compiled visual intent (style 'tabular', density 'balanced', rhythm 'even', alignment 'loose')  validated against the runtime's schema.
Values on this screen are illustrative, not live telemetry.

Outranked on the weighted total (6 vs 6.48). when how things connect is the decision, the connections must be drawn, not described in rows (explore decision, service links,replication status per node,dependency depth,downtime,requests per hour,load balance quota,history of the last failure item(s)). taskFit: 6 — ranked affinity for the 'explore' decision class, plus the brief's stated relationships that this family draws. relationshipClarity: 9 — 3 stated relationship item(s): 'service links', 'replication status per node', 'dependency depth' — drawn, not listed. informationHierarchy: 8 — 7 information item(s) against a spatial field: dense past ~8 nodes, individual labels stop being readable in place. densityScanability: 6 — how 7 item(s) sit in this family: spaced nodes need room per label.
